## Design

### 2026-11-01: Schematic done

**3h**

Schematic done

Today I drew the schematic for my OLED Pixel Face board in KiCad.

The board has an ESP32 DevKit V1, a small OLED screen and two buttons. The OLED talks to the ESP32 with just two wires, SDA on GPIO21 and SCL on GPIO22. It also gets 3.3V and ground from the ESP32.

The two buttons go to GPIO25 and GPIO26, and the other side of each button goes to ground. I did not add resistors, because the ESP32 has built-in pull-ups that I turn on in the code.

I added a small 100 nF capacitor near the OLED power to keep the voltage steady. It is optional, but it is cheap.

I ran the KiCad electrical rules check and it shows 0 errors. Next I will design the PCB layout.

### 2026-11-01: PCB layout done

**4h**

PCB layout done

Today I designed the PCB for my OLED Pixel Face. It is a small 60 x 54 mm two-layer board with rounded corners and four M3 mounting holes.

The ESP32 plugs into two rows of female headers, so I can take it off. The OLED plugs into a 4-pin socket (GND, VCC, SCL, SDA), and the two buttons sit on the board. I used through-hole parts so I can solder it by hand.

I spent most of the time placing parts and routing the traces. I kept the I2C lines (SDA and SCL) short and put the buttons near the edge so they are easy to press. The bottom layer is a ground plane, and the top layer has a ground pour joined with vias. This keeps the wiring simple and the ground solid.

For the buttons I wired only two diagonal pads. On a 4-leg button, two legs on one side are joined inside, and different datasheets disagree on which. Using diagonal pads means it works whichever way the button is paired and can never be shorted.

I used 22.86 mm between the two ESP32 header rows. Clone boards vary, so I will measure my real board before ordering.

The KiCad design rule check shows 0 errors, 0 unconnected items, and the PCB matches the schematic.

### 2026-11-01: Firmware done

**3h**

Firmware done

Today I got the firmware for my OLED Pixel Face working. It is an Arduino sketch for the ESP32.

I installed ESP32 support in Arduino IDE, added the Adafruit SSD1306 and Adafruit GFX libraries, and set the board to ESP32 Dev Module.

The code draws each face from big pixel blocks, so it looks like pixel art. There are four faces: happy, surprised, sleepy and curious. The awake faces blink at random times, and sleep mode shows closed eyes with floating “Zzz”.

The Next button (GPIO25) changes the face, and holding it goes back one face. The Sleep button (GPIO26) puts the screen to sleep, and holding it turns automatic mode on or off. In automatic mode the face changes by itself every 2.5 seconds.

The buttons use the ESP32’s built-in pull-ups, so I did not need any resistors. The OLED uses I2C on GPIO21 and GPIO22.

The code compiled with no errors. I tested the faces and buttons in the Wokwi simulator, wired the same way as my schematic.
